content.head:
# MinIO, or any other S3-compatible endpoint reached by hostname.
#
# cf-deployment v59.0.0 moved cloud_controller off the fog gem onto
# storage-cli and stripped the fog_connection wiring out of
# operations/use-external-blobstore.yml, which now sets only the four directory
# keys. The wiring below replaces that fog_connection block and has to be
# declared on each of the three cloud_controller jobs.
#
# Property names come from capi's jobs/cloud_controller_ng/templates/
# storage_cli_config_<bucket>.json.erb, not from storage-cli's own config
# struct. For provider s3 the template reads bucket_name, aws_access_key_id,
# and aws_secret_access_key, sets credentials_source itself, and passes host,
# port, region, use_ssl, ssl_verify_peer, and host_style through when present.
# Writing storage-cli's internal names, access_key_id and secret_access_key,
# renders nothing and fails the deploy on a missing property.
#
# Two things an operator has to act on when upgrading.
#
# blobstore_minio_endpoint is gone. storage-cli takes a bare hostname and a
# separate port, and it builds the endpoint itself from host, port, and
# use_ssl, so there is nowhere to put a URL. Split the old value into
# blobstore_minio_host, blobstore_minio_port, and blobstore_minio_use_ssl. An
# environment that still carries only the old parameter fails to render, with
# the message on blobstore_minio_host below.
#
# Signature version 2 is gone as well. The fog configuration pinned
# aws_signature_version to 2, and storage-cli has no such setting. capi's
# template forwards a signature_version key, but storage-cli's S3 config struct
# has no field to receive it and drops it, signing every request with version
# 4. MinIO has spoken version 4 for years, so this should be invisible, but an
# endpoint that genuinely only accepts version 2 can no longer be reached.
#
# storage-cli has no ssl_ca_file knob, so a private CA has to reach the VM's
# system trust store, which on a Genesis foundation means the os-conf ca_certs
# runtime config. Where that is not in place, set blobstore_minio_ssl_verify_peer
# to false rather than expecting a CA parameter.

content.value: (( param "Specify the hostname of the MinIO endpoint to use as your Cloud Controller blobstore. This replaces blobstore_minio_endpoint, because storage-cli takes a bare hostname rather than a URL. Give the host on its own here, and set blobstore_minio_port and blobstore_minio_use_ssl separately." ))

# storage-cli names bucket addressing the opposite way round from fog.
# host_style false is the path style the fog configuration asked for, and it
# is what a MinIO deployment without wildcard DNS needs.

# MinIO ignores the region but the AWS signing algorithm does not, and the
# empty string the fog configuration used is not a valid one. us-east-1 is
# what MinIO itself defaults to.
